verdict.rationale: WorkOS documents M2M applications for issuing programmatic API access credentials (workos-docs-32), and AuthKit acts as a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server for securing MCP servers (workos-docs-27, workos-docs-8). Combined with RBAC roles and permissions enforced through session JWTs (workos-docs-3, workos-supp-rbac-jwt), this gives a plausible path to least-privilege agent access. However, the evidence never explicitly shows per-credential scopes for agents, and WorkOS's own MCP server lets an agent change the same dashboard data the user can (workos-docs-44), which suggests broad rather than least-privilege access for its own workspace. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of scoping M2M or OAuth tokens to specific permissions, agent-specific least-privilege credential guidance, scoped access for WorkOS's own MCP or API keys, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
